RLHF by hand ✍️ ~ 15 steps walkthrough below

Train a model on human text and it inherits human bias. It will assume a doctor is a "him", because the data says so.

RLHF is the correction. A human marks one preference, doc is them over doc is him, and the weights move.

But one correction is not the point. The hope is that the model learns the value behind it, gender neutrality, and applies it to professions nobody ever mentioned.

How does it work?

Goal: train a reward model from a single human comparison about doctors, then turn it on CEOs, filling in every cell yourself.

= 1. Given =

A reward model, an LLM, and two (prompt, next) pairs.

= 2. Preferences =

A human reads both pairs and picks a winner: (doc is, them) beats (doc is, him). The loser is not bad grammar, it is gender bias, and that is the whole signal.

= 3. Word embeddings =

Let us look up each word of the loser pair. These vectors are the reward model's input.

= 4. Linear layer =

We multiply by the reward model's weights and add its biases. Out come feature vectors, one per position.

= 5. Mean pool =

Let us multiply by [1/3, 1/3, 1/3], which averages the three positions into one sentence embedding.

= 6. Output layer =

We map that sentence down to a single number. Reward = 3.

= 7. The winner, the same way =

Let us repeat steps 3 to 6 on the winning pair. Reward = 5.

= 8. Winner minus loser =

We take the gap: 5 - 3 = 2. The reward model wants this positive and as large as it can make it.

= 9. Loss gradient =

Let us squash the gap into a probability, σ(2) ≈ 0.9, and subtract the target of 1. The gradient is -0.1, and it goes back through the purple weights. The reward model is now trained.

= 10. A prompt it has never seen =

We start the second half with "[S] CEO is". The feedback in step 2 was about doctors. Nothing connects a CEO to a doctor except what the reward model generalised.

= 11. Transformer =

Let us push it through attention and a feed forward layer, one vector per position.

= 12. Output probabilities =

We map each vector to a score over the vocabulary.

= 13. Sample =

Let us take the highest score. The model completes "CEO is" with "him", which is the same bias the human penalised in step 2.

= 14. Score it with the reward model =

We feed the new pair (CEO is, him) through steps 3 to 6. Reward = 3, exactly the score it gave "doc is him" in step 6. Nobody taught it about CEOs. The value transferred.

= 15. Loss gradient =

Let us set the loss to the negative of the reward, so minimising the loss maximises the reward. The gradient is a constant -1, and it goes back through the red weights.

The outputs:
Loser reward = 3, winner reward = 5
Reward gap = 2, predicted σ ≈ 0.9, reward model gradient = -0.1
LLM samples "him", reward = 3, LLM gradient = -1

Congrats! You just calculated RLHF by hand.

And you watched a value generalise: one comparison about doctors, and the model marks down "CEO is him" unprompted.

If I had to start Python again in 2026, this is the exact roadmap I'd follow👇
🐍 Python Master Cheatsheet (2026)
1. Basics
Learn variables, indentation, comments, input/output, and Python syntax. This is the foundation—skip it and everything else feels confusing.
2. Data Types
Understand integers, floats, strings, booleans, lists, tuples, sets, and dictionaries. Every Python program is built on these.
3. Operators
Master arithmetic, comparison, logical, and assignment operators to perform calculations and make decisions.
4. Control Flow
Use if, elif, else, for, and while loops to control how your program behaves.
5. Functions
Write reusable code with def, parameters, return values, default arguments, and clean function design.
6. Strings
Manipulate text using slicing, formatting, .split(), .join(), .replace(), and f-strings.
7. Lists
Store collections of data. Learn indexing, slicing, appending, removing, sorting, and looping.
8. Tuples
Immutable collections that are faster and safer when your data shouldn't change.
9. Sets
Remove duplicates, perform unions/intersections, and speed up lookups.
10. Dictionaries
Store data as key-value pairs. Essential for APIs, JSON, and real-world applications.
11. List Comprehensions
Write cleaner and more Pythonic code in a single line.
12. Lambda Functions
Create small anonymous functions for sorting, filtering, and quick operations.
13. File Handling
Read, write, and manage files using open(), with, and file modes.
14. Exception Handling
Use try, except, finally, and raise so your programs don't crash unexpectedly.
15. Modules
Leverage Python's standard library (math, os, datetime, random) instead of reinventing the wheel.
16. Built-in Functions
Master len(), sum(), range(), sorted(), max(), min() and dozens more to write efficient code.
17. Pip
Install and manage packages like NumPy, Pandas, Requests, and Flask with ease.
18. Virtual Environments
Keep project dependencies isolated to avoid version conflicts.
19. Magic (Dunder) Methods
Learn __init__, __str__, __repr__, and more to write professional object-oriented Python.
20. Best Practices
Write readable code, follow PEP 8, use meaningful names, handle errors, and build projects consistently.
📌 Master these 20 topics, and you'll have a strong Python foundation for: • AI & Machine Learning • Data Science • Automation • Web Development • Backend APIs • Cybersecurity

MiniMax H3 is really impressive for commercial creation.

Creating ads with AI is becoming a completely different experience. With multimodal references, you can combine images, videos, audio, and text to build more consistent and controllable visuals.

Up to 12 references + native 2K generation makes H3 a powerful tool for bringing advertising ideas to life.

- Create a premium 9:16 fashion-eyewear commercial. Match the reference video’s shot rhythm, edit speed, white-cyclorama look, and severe fashion attitude. Use a seamless minimal white studio with clean, bold, avant-garde art direction worthy of a global luxury campaign.

Most health apps just show you boring charts, but Sleepagotchi turns your rest into a fun game.

 When you go to bed on time and hit your sleep goals, you get digital rewards every morning. 

You can use your rewards to grow your cute Dino pet, collect hero cards, and fix up your virtual room.

It syncs with your Apple Watch, Oura, or WHOOP, so tracking is super easy. 

On top of that, there is a smart AI coach inside the app to give you simple tips for better rest and daily health.
